children: Sen.
Mark Kelly
(D-Ariz) called on the public to help the
National Aeronautics and Space Administration
(NASA) identify key human-health questions as NASA plans for longer-duration human missions on the Moon.
NASA Seeks Input on Astronaut Health Risks
On Saturday, in a post on
X
, Kelly shared a post from NASA Moon Base and urged the public to contribute research questions that could help shape future lunar missions.
"Science is about asking questions," he wrote. "NASA is studying the impact of space on human health as astronauts prepare to spend more time living and working on the Moon."
He added, "If you have ideas about what they should focus on, NASA wants to hear them."
NASA Wants Astronaut Health Data, Technology
NASA said it is seeking input to help shape human health and performance research for a future Moon Base.
The agency wants suggestions on research questions that should be explored as astronauts spend more time on the lunar surface.
It is also seeking recommendations on what health and performance data should be collected during early Moon Base development missions.
NASA is additionally asking for ideas on technologies and capabilities that could support the research.
